newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Today's inauguration of the natural gas network project is the green light for a series of important Greek-Russian energy investments that will significantly bolster Greece's strategic role in the region. Yesterday's meeting between Prime Minister Costas Simitis and the visiting Russian energy minister led to the signing of an energy cooperation protocol.
--OTE, Greece's telecommunications organisation, will draft and work with the national economy and finance ministry on its proposal for a second share offer.

--A new round of farmers' protests is expected to be slated for early February at tomorrow's meeting of farmers in Lamia. At the moment, farmers are drafting the specifics of their demands, to be put to the government.
--The government will have decided on the Bank of Piraeus's offer for the Bank of Crete by Friday, sources say.

--A wave of vessels are preparing to leave the Greek registry, due to shipowners' estimations that the flag is no longer competitive due to high operating costs. The fleet fell by 112 vessels last year.
--Greek-Russian energy cooperation in electrical energy, petroleum, the chemical industry and natural gas works well with Greek plans to become an energy hub for the Balkans.
--The drachma's slide against the Ecu yesterday was an indication of the Bank of Greece's future handling of exchange policy.
--The Bank of Piraeus's offer for the Bank of Crete has officials concerned about the manner in which it has offered to pay.
--The energy market is opening to the private sector, as part of Development Minister Vasso Papandreou's Balkans campaign.
--OTE's investment programme this year, apart from a new share offer of between 8-10 percent, also sees 240 billion drachmas in investments.
--The development ministry's general secretariat for consumers is nearing the final stretch but doubts have arisen over whether a quality food control team will eventually be established.
--The first series of two-year zero coupons will be issued next Monday with an interest rate of 10.5 percent. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
